Historical Materialism: Base and Superstructure
The Political Superstructure
Man's social knowledge-political
institutions, laws, religion, and
philosophical doctrines.
Man's social knowledge reflects
the economic system.
The Economic System (The Base]
The growth of productive forces. This exists
independently of man and dictates the structure of
society (e.g., capitalism growing out of feudalism).
Application Note
Various political forms of modern
European states serve explicitly to
strengthen the domination of the
bourgeoisie over the proletariat.

PILLAR II:
Economics
Having recognized that the economic system is
the foundation... Marx devoted his greatest
attention to the study of this economic system in
his principal work, Capital.
Classical political economy evolved in England
(the most developed capitalist country). Adam
Smith and David Ricardo laid the foundations
of the Labour Theory of Value.
Marx provided the proof. He demonstrated that
the value of every commodity is determined by
the quantity of socially necessary labour time
spent on its production.

PILLAR III: Socialism
When feudalism was overthrown...
it at once became apparent that this
"freedom" meant a new svstem
of oppression and exploitation.
The stormy revolutions across Europe (especially in France)
accompanying the fall of serfdom clearly revealed the hidden driver
of human history. Not a single victory for political freedom was
won except against desperate resistance. Not a single capitalist
country evolved without a life-and-death struggle between classes.

From Utopian to Scientific Socialism
Early Utopian Socialism
Bridge/Spectrum
Marxist Scientific Socialism
Method: Criticized, condemned, and damned
capitalist society.
Action: Dreamed of a better order; endeavored
to convince the rich of the immorality of
exploitation.
Fatal Flaw: Could not explain wage-slavery,
reveal the laws of development, or indicate the
social force capable of creating a new society.
Method: Deduced the mechanical lesson of world
history.
Action: Replaced dreams with the doctrine of the
class struggle.
The Solution: Identified the specific forces within
the surrounding society that must sweep away the
old and create the new.

The Mechanics of Deception
The Facade:
Moral, religious, political, and
social phrases, declarations, and
promises. Champions of reform
and improvements.
The Reality: The forces of
certain ruling classes
protecting rotten institutions
Lenin's Law of Politics: People always have been the foolish victims of deception and
self-deception in politics, and they always will be until they have learnt to seek out the
interests of some class or other behind all moral, religious, political and social phrases.
The Only Way Out: To smash the resistance of these classes by enlightening and
organizing the oppressed forces for the struggle.
